endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: When AI-enabled technologies are acquired from a third party, local validation and installation qualification need to be conducted first, prior to the assessment of the AI system.

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions: Lifecycle Management and Marketing Submission Recommendations (draft guidance)
endorsements.quote: Software verification and validation testing was conducted and documentation 2224 was provided as recommended in the Premarket Software Guidance.

endorsements.title: Considerations for the regulation of generative AI-enabled medical devices (discussion paper)
endorsements.quote: Such evaluation has traditionally relied on extensive testing across a representative sample of device inputs and outputs; for GenAI-enabled devices, the range of possible inputs and outputs may be too large for such testing to be practical.

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
endorsements.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
endorsements.quote: Institute test and evaluation for data and content flows within the GAI system, including but not limited to, original data sources, data transformations, and decision-making criteria.

endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Are AI outputs (including embedded features) periodically spot-checked and reflected in enterprise reporting?

endorsements.title: Choosing the right artificial intelligence solutions for your radiology department: key factors to consider
endorsements.quote: Trial integration and IT assessment: Conduct a trial integration of the AI solution with the assistance of IT professionals to identify potential compliance or technical issues before full implementation.

endorsements.title: Achieving health equity through conversational AI: A roadmap for design and implementation of inclusive chatbots in healthcare
endorsements.quote: It is important to conduct integration testing to ensure that conversational AI data exchange is continuous and accurate, particularly when conversational AI access electronic health records, appointment booking systems, prescription, and medication support systems where patient details are stored.

endorsements.title: Artificial intelligence in echocardiography: a position statement from the British Society of Echocardiography
endorsements.quote: This workflow introduces further dependencies on secure, high‑bandwidth connectivity, robust cybersecurity safeguards, and clear data‑transfer agreements. These requirements may pose challenges for centres with limited digital capacity or restrictive information‑governance policies and must therefore be factored into local readiness assessments.

evidence.title: Real-World Evaluation of AI-Driven Diabetic Retinopathy Screening in Public Health Settings: Validation and Implementation Study
evidence.outcome: Two-week pre-implementation integration testing of hardware, connectivity, workflow
evidence.effect: Testing identified technical issues and bottlenecks, leading to improved connectivity, mandatory clinical variables, faster turnaround, and local data storage.
evidence.quote: The two-week testing at PGIMER and DH Mohali validated the full AI workflow, identified technical issues, assessed reliability in clinical settings, and highlighted data and reporting bottlenecks.

evidence.title: Implementation of an artificial intelligence-based system for mammography in the compulsory medical insurance program: results of a 3-year study
evidence.venue: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
evidence.outcome: Detection of incomplete mammogram processing during predeployment functional testing
evidence.effect: Functional testing identified incomplete processing in one out of four mammography studies, prompting developer refinement.
evidence.quote: Functional testing identified one critical noncompliance: one out of four mammography studies was processed incompletely.

evidence.title: In vivo clinical effectiveness of artificial intelligence screening for acute coronary syndrome: testing real-world performance
evidence.outcome: Technical component analysis of CDS population capture, calculation, threshold, data capture
evidence.effect: No errors in population capture, risk calculation, threshold, or decision alignment; data capture for monitoring found to record overwritten values, not data used by CDS; corrected
evidence.quote: In the evaluation of the data capture for monitoring and transparency, we discovered that the ‘live care’ data that was recorded in the report were not what the CDS used for its calculations.

evidence.title: In vitro to in vivo translation of artificial intelligence for clinical use: screening for acute coronary syndrome to identify ST-elevation myocardial infarction
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Technical component testing of CDS coding before activation
evidence.effect: Technical Component Analysis identified several small coding errors in CDS components, which were addressed.
evidence.quote: The Technical Component Analysis indicated several small coding errors in CDS components that were addressed.

evidence.title: Benchmarking of radiobiological NTCP models in head and neck radiotherapy using independent computational pipelines: an institutional validation study with machine learning augmentation
evidence.outcome: Agreement between two independent NTCP computational pipelines against predefined acceptance criteria
evidence.effect: Mean bias 0.8%, 95% limits of agreement -1.9% to +3.5%, meeting predefined criteria (bias <3%, limits within ±5%); max deviation 2.4%.
evidence.quote: The mean bias was 0.8%, with 95% limits of agreement ranging from −1.9% to +3.5%, meeting the predefined acceptability criteria (mean bias <3% and limits within ±5%).

evidence.title: AI-based automatic patient positioning in a digital-BGO PET/CT scanner: efficacy and impact
evidence.outcome: Off-centering >2.5 cm before vs after correcting camera mounting-angle installation error
evidence.effect: Before recalibration, AI positioning was no better than manual (49% vs 54% of studies off-centered >2.5 cm). After recalibration, 27% (38/140), p<0.001.
evidence.quote: With respect to off-centering measurements, although there was not any significant difference between the AI and manual methods before the positioning camera recalibration, afterwards the number of studies with greater than 2.5 cm off-centering dropped from about one-half to one-quarter, confirming its efficacy for PET/CT.

evidence.title: Leveraging AI to Drive Timely Improvements in Patient Experience Feedback: Algorithm Validation
evidence.effect: Common errors were “FileNotFoundError” from incorrect .pkl paths and “invalid column name” from SQL input-column mismatch before final deployment.
evidence.quote: The 2 most common errors encountered were “FileNotFoundError” which was a result of not specifying the correct path to a .pkl file, and “invalid column name,” as the code had not been adapted appropriately with the column names from the input table on the SQL server.
evidence.sample_unit: NHS trusts (500-comment stratified manually coded sample per trust for accuracy)

evidence.title: From Offline Accuracy to Deployed Performance: A Four-Phase Evaluation of an Edge-Hosted Wearable Stress-Monitoring Platform
evidence.outcome: Serving-layer completion rate under 50-worker burst load
evidence.effect: 86.8% completion rate under 50-worker burst load; serving layer identified as the concurrency bottleneck. Mean sequential latency 80.47 ms (p95 84.86 ms).
evidence.quote: Phase 1 measured a mean sequential HTTP latency of 80.47 milliseconds (ms) (95th percentile [p95] = 84.86 ms), isolated route-level timing across the Machine Learning (ML)-only, Deep Learning (DL)-only, and hybrid paths, and exposed an 86.8% completion rate under 50-worker burst load, thereby identifying the serving layer as the current concurrency bottleneck.
evidence.sample_unit: real WESAD stress windows (Phase 2 sensor-loss test)

commentary.bottom_line: Four studies report that pre-go-live testing found integration, processing, coding, or monitoring-data faults that were then corrected, and a fifth reports that two computational pipelines met predefined acceptance criteria. None compared go-live failures or patient harm between tested and untested deployments, and none tested acceptance checks of load capacity or provenance mechanisms.

perspectives.view: Before deployment, functional testing found incomplete processing in one of four mammography studies. In another study, testing found that the monitoring log recorded overwritten values instead of the data the tool used. A camera mounting-angle error left 49% of PET/CT studies off-centered until recalibration cut this to 27%, which suggests installation faults can reach patients.

Component-level checks of population capture, risk calculation, thresholds, and CDS coding found small coding errors and a monitoring data-capture fault in live EHR settings. Across nine NHS trusts, common deployment script errors involved file paths and SQL column mismatches. One offline burst-load test reached 86.8% completion, but no study tested load acceptance as a go-live gate.

One rural safety-net deployment used a two-week integration test of hardware, connectivity, and workflow. The test led to improved connectivity, mandatory clinical variables, faster turnaround, and local data storage. No study reported the staff time or cost of acceptance testing, so leaders cannot yet weigh its burden against avoided failures.

CHAI states that installation qualification must come before assessment of a third-party AI system, and NIST advises testing data and content flows. FDA draft guidance describes manufacturer verification and validation, which does not replace local acceptance testing. An FDA discussion paper notes that input-output testing may be impractical for generative AI devices.

The one study set in safety-net and rural sites found connectivity and workflow bottlenecks during pre-implementation testing. The echocardiography position statement warns that bandwidth and data-transfer requirements may strain centres with limited digital capacity. Evidence from low-resource sites therefore rests on a single deployment in India.

commentary.research_gap: No study compared go-live failure rates, downtime, or patient harm between deployments that did and did not undergo acceptance testing. No study tested acceptance checks for load capacity, provenance mechanisms, or monitoring alert logic, and none reported the cost or staff time of testing.
commentary.underserved_note: Only one test (pmid:40925861) included safety-net and rural populations, and it took place in India. No test reported Medicaid, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. The results may therefore not transfer to U.S. safety-net systems or to interfaces used by patients with language or literacy barriers.
